title: Stronger with every update: How we’re making Chrome and the web safer in the AI Era
excerpt: Chrome uses Gemini AI to automate vulnerability discovery, triage, and patching, accelerating updates to match modern security risks.

How Chrome is using AI to improve vulnerability discovery, triage, and patching.

Chrome Security Team

We’re living through a massive shift in the software security industry. Large Language Models (LLMs) are unlocking unprecedented capabilities for automated vulnerability discovery, scaling far beyond the limits of human security expertise, and requiring new approaches for staying ahead of attackers.

This means deploying AI models at scale to find and fix hundreds of security bugs, faster than ever, with the goal of achieving greater resilience and comprehensive remediation.

Here’s how we’re doing it.

The Life of A Bug

Some software bugs have security implications. While a purely functional bug might result in a frustrating UI freeze, a security bug (or vulnerability) can be used to build an exploit. Exploits allow attackers to perform malicious actions on a victim’s computer, such as reading private data, or controlling their machine without their knowledge.

Once a security bug enters the codebase, its life cycle proceeds as follows:

  • The bug is found.
  • The bug is triaged.
  • The bug is fixed.
  • A new update of Chrome with the bug fix is released.
  • Chrome is restarted and the update is applied.

Our goal is for every one of these steps to happen as quickly as possible.

Finding vulnerabilities

The Chrome Security team has been using LLMs for years. In 2023 we developed ways to use LLMs to increase security fuzzing coverage and performance. In 2024, we worked with Project Zero on Naptime, giving LLMs specialized tools for vulnerability research. And in 2025, we collaborated with DeepMind and Project Zero on Big Sleep, an AI vulnerability discovery agent that successfully found bugs in the V8 JavaScript engine and graphics stack.

In early 2026, we built an agent harness that used Gemini to find vulnerabilities across the broader Chrome codebase with higher efficiency and lower false positives. One of the bugs we found was a sandbox escape that would allow a compromised renderer to trick the browser into reading local files — a bug that quietly survived in our codebase for more than 13 years! For many of us, this moment cemented the potential of AI-powered vulnerability detection.

From there, we improved on our vulnerability finding agent harness by:

  • Adding support for model interoperability to leverage the unique strengths of both open-weights and proprietary models.
  • Building a knowledge base of Chrome, including all previously identified CVEs and Chrome’s entire Git history, to extend the LLMs reasoning capacity past its training data.
  • Encouraging developers to add SECURITY.md files, which help models better understand trust boundaries and develop an accurate view of the threat model.
  • Adding a “critic” agent with a separate context to consume these SECURITY.md files.
  • Introducing the ability to run vulnerability finding models over the codebase multiple times to account for model non-determinism and model improvements over time.

We’ve built all of this with safety in mind, and have put in place guardrails to mitigate the risk of AI behaving unexpectedly. Our AI analyzes source code strictly at rest, operating on locked-down machines that lack general internet access. We also utilize a dedicated setup for these internal scans that intercepts all network requests, employing strict allowlists based on the initiating application and destination, blocking any suspicious model activity. Furthermore, we never run models in an unrestricted mode, and we strictly limit our subagents from modifying the local system or accessing files outside of designated source code directories.

AI-powered vulnerability detection complements our existing security testing infrastructure. For example, fuzzing continues to be especially effective at finding bugs that arise from long-range interactions between disparate parts of our codebase, or those requiring a combination of seemingly unrelated operations.

We also want to continue to reward external researchers for their expertise and creativity in finding the most challenging and impactful vulnerabilities via the Chrome Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP). In early 2026, we saw a gradual increase in all categories of bug reports, but by March, the shift was apparent: we received more bug reports than we had in the entirety of 2025. This led us to change our VRP to focus researchers on bug submissions that are additive to what we are finding internally, and easily ingestible by our newly automated processing pipelines.

Triaging vulnerabilities

As we discover more security vulnerabilities with AI-powered tools, we’ve simultaneously used AI to scale and automate validating, triaging, and fixing bugs. Historically, triaging a single security report took anywhere from 5 to 30 or more minutes, and relied primarily on human expertise. We have been increasingly shifting our triage process towards an automated approach that blends rule-based systems with AI to increase throughput and accuracy.

The automated triage process is broken down into four key phases:

  1. Filtering out the noise. The system checks if an incoming bug is spam, ensures it meets intake criteria (e.g. is not a duplicate), and verifies that it clearly describes a Chrome security vulnerability.
  2. Reproducing bugs. Next, the system checks for a proof of concept. Reproducible bugs are tested on the specific operating system and browser versions they affect. Based on this, the system attaches further details such as stack traces to the bug to help inform the fix.
  3. Enriching the report with metadata. The system adds essential metadata to the report, such as when the bug was first introduced and its severity rating. To help this process scale, we’ve made our severity guidelines clearer and easier to apply automatically. We continue to allow developers to modify the severity rating if they believe it is incorrect, and to add context to help models reason about security boundaries using SECURITY.md files.
  4. Automatic assigning. The system automatically routes the issue to the correct component and human owner.

While it's hard to measure precisely, we estimate that this new process is saving hundreds of hours of developer time per month, allowing our team to focus on other security priorities.

Fixing vulnerabilities

Across Google, developers share the responsibility of prioritizing security fixes with the security team, but scaling bug discovery requires an equally scalable bug fixing process.

To achieve this, we rely on multi-agent workflows throughout:

  • After initial build steps that bring in context from a specific issue, we run a fixing agent that returns multiple candidate fixes.
  • A critic agent then evaluates which would be the best fit, producing other relevant artifacts for developers to evaluate the fix.
  • The fixing and critic agents work in a loop that mimics a typical code review process to ensure that code is functional and compliant with Chromium and Google style guidelines, as well as other local code conventions.
  • Test-writing agents help write tests for fixes. These agents can ensure that tests work across the full array of Chrome supported platforms and configurations before a developer reviews the fix, saving up to weeks of developer time.

At this point, we have LLMs generating candidate fixes for most vulnerabilities, dramatically increasing the rate of security fixes in recent Chrome releases:

Number of security bugs fixed in recent Chrome Stable release milestones

In the last two milestones, Chrome 149 and 150, we have fixed 1072 security bugs, surpassing the total number of security bugs fixed across the prior 23 milestones combined.

We have partnered closely with Google DeepMind and Project Zero for years, including on BigSleep and CodeMender. These tools are natively integrated into our continuous integration (CI) system, running every 24 hours across all CLs to proactively detect security bugs. This integration has yielded significant results: in May alone, we blocked over 20 vulnerabilities from reaching production, including a critical S1+ issue.

Releasing fixes

Once a fix has landed and is visible in the public open source codebase, attackers can start to reverse engineer and exploit the bug before the fix reaches users’ machines — so called "N-day" attacks. This is commonly referred to as the “patch gap.” Since fixes committed to the main “tree” typically take weeks to reach the Chrome Stable channel (what the vast majority of our users run), minimizing this patch gap is a critical part of our strategy.

Based on their severity, security fixes are merged directly from the main “tree” into the active Chrome stable release branch, which is continuously monitored to prevent new crashes or regressions. We are in the process of transitioning to a two-week cadence for major Chrome milestones, with weekly security updates. However, in the face of fast-moving, AI-powered attacks, our delivery cadence must accelerate even further. To meet this moment, we are piloting a shift to two security releases per week.

Even with this pace, proper public disclosure remains paramount. Every security bug that reaches Chrome Stable, regardless of whether it was discovered internally or reported externally, is documented and disclosed publicly as a standard best practice. We are working on automating the generation of release notes and CVE descriptions from security bug fixes to eliminate manual bottlenecks and shorten the window between vulnerability discovery and public disclosure.

Applying updates

In 2008, Chrome pioneered the concept of silent, background software updates: new binaries are automatically downloaded and staged on disk with minimal user intervention. At the next restart of the browser, the update would be applied and the user would be protected. However, compared to the 1–2 days it takes for triage, fix, test and release, the time spent waiting for the user to restart Chrome can be a significant contributor to N-day exploitation risk.

People have understandable reasons to delay restarting Chrome. A restart can be disruptive, requires scheduling in-between tasks, and is rarely the top priority at any given moment. To eliminate this friction, we are pioneering ways to shift the burden away from the user by:

  • Investing in "dynamic patching" that will eliminate the need for a full browser restart in most cases. By leveraging Chrome’s multi-process architecture, dynamic patching sequentially replaces background child processes (like the Renderer and GPU) with updated binaries on the fly. Stay tuned to learn more as we research and develop this feature.
  • Exploring ways to ensure a seamless session restore even in complex cases, by saving more state locally.
  • Finding opportune moments to restart automatically, when we can guarantee a seamless session restore. For example, in Chrome 150, we rolled out a change to take advantage of the unique application state on macOS where applications typically continue running in the background even after all windows are closed. Now, if Chrome detects a pending update while in this windowless state, it automatically restarts.

Zero window auto-restart on macOS

Our long-term vision is a browser that is always up-to-date – continuously and dynamically patched, and automatically restarted during opportune periods of minimal disruption. While we’re working on this, you can keep your Chrome up to date by clicking on the update message in the top right corner.

For enterprise customers looking to keep Chrome up to date, we recommend that IT admins:

  • Apply the RelaunchNotification policy which prompts users to restart Chrome to apply a pending update, escalating from a gentle reminder to a forced restart over a set timeframe.
  • Utilize the Chrome Extended Stable Channel for highly sensitive environments where software changes must be vetted.
  • Leverage the OS-agnostic dashboard provided by Chrome Enterprise Core or Premium to track fleet-wide browser versions and manage updates at a more granular level.

Prevention is better than cure

Beyond fixing individual security bugs, we’re also investing in the mitigation and elimination of entire classes of security bugs, as well as in preventing them from landing in the first place. With AI coding advancements, we believe there are exciting opportunities to accelerate projects that would have previously taken years, or never happened.

Memory safety mitigations

Chrome is executing on a two-layered memory safety strategy: hardening our runtime environment to neutralize legacy C++ vulnerabilities, while shifting to memory-safe languages for long-term architectural resilience.

The vast majority of the Chromium codebase remains in C++, making immediate toolchain and runtime mitigations our critical first line of defense. We have long prioritized memory-safety engineering at scale, deploying hardened standard template libraries and pioneering technologies like the MiraclePtr family to neutralize Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerabilities. AI-powered vulnerability detection only reaffirms the need for such technology.

Our C++ defensive roadmap is focused on three pillars:

  • MiraclePtr & MiracleObject Expansion. Having already driven a major reduction in UAF bugs via MiraclePtr, we are expanding this paradigm to more libraries such as Skia, ANGLE, Dawn, C++ iterators and std:: containers. We are also actively deploying MiracleObject with the aim of neutralizing up to 90% of UAF vulnerabilities on the GPU main thread, deliberately trading localized runtime performance for temporal safety.
  • Spanification. To systematically eliminate Out-of-Bounds (OOB) spatial safety errors, Chrome has undertaken a massive "spanification" effort, migrating legacy pointer-and-size constructs to compiler-enforced std::span types. Currently, 97% of first-party Chrome code compiles cleanly with strict unsafe-buffer warnings. We are now pushing these requirements downstream, expanding spanification into foundational codebases like Skia, ANGLE, and Dawn.
  • Structural & Allocation Hardening. We are working on integrating checked math for calculations tied to memory allocations to block integer overflow avenues. Concurrently, Chrome is implementing an additional level of heap partitioning to strictly segregate pointer-containing types from non-pointer types to make it harder to exploit UAF bugs.

While C++ safety enhancements provide an immediate shield, we believe that runtime mitigations will hit diminishing marginal returns within the next few years. Runtime checks are inherently more expensive than compile-time guarantees, and even a heavily mitigated C++ binary requires rigid, performance-throttling sandboxing to comply with the Rule of Two.

The long-term solution is shifting the codebase towards memory-safe languages like Rust, focusing on the following core tenets:

  • Rust flywheel. Developers cannot be expected to entirely absorb the velocity friction of engineering in a new language ecosystem. As such, we are building a centralized Rust SDK that exposes foundational Chromium APIs and tooling directly to Rust. Our aim is to turn Rust into a routine, frictionless engineering choice for new components.
  • Targeted “bug nest” eradication. Rust is being deployed strategically to replace code segments that exhibit high historical bug density (such as complex data parsers, image codecs, and font stacks).
  • Enabling high-privilege modularization. By writing new modular components in Rust, Chrome can safely execute complex features inside high-privilege processes (like the browser process) without the performance penalties of sandboxing, breaking the constraints of traditional C++ architecture.

In addition to Rust, we are also exploring options like implementing the browser’s top-level user interface using HTML, CSS, and TypeScript to further reduce dependencies on traditional C++ frameworks.

Catching security bugs before they land

Bulk scanning of a code base cannot keep pace with Chrome’s high-traffic development velocity. To account for this, we’re also deploying AI-powered bug-finding capabilities to identify and prevent bugs as close to code submit-time as possible. Part of Chrome’s continuous integration (CI) and commit queue (CQ) pipeline, these defensive models automatically scan diffs to prevent new vulnerabilities by performing actions like suggesting spanification fixes, flagging dangling pointers, and enforcing numeric safety.

Additionally, a major challenge in large-scale software engineering is the “latent security issue.” Code that is safe and robust in isolation can be transformed into a critical vulnerability by an entirely unrelated, minor logic change elsewhere in the tree. By utilizing continuous, LLM-powered semantic analysis within the CQ, Chrome can intercept these compound risks before they land in the tree, catching the subtle or complex interactions that traditional static analysis misses.

Securing the internet

Keeping the web safe involves more than just securing Chrome. Google has been a long-standing supporter of open source projects and communities to ensure better security outcomes for all users. Most recently, Google joined others in donating $12.5M to the Alpha-Omega project in support of enabling maintainers to have access to the tools and support they will need in order to respond quickly to vulnerability reports. Google was also a founding member of the Akrites project, which aims to lower the burden on upstream maintainers by providing a centralized clearinghouse for vulnerability reports and a security incident response team.

On the Chrome team, we feel this responsibility acutely — the Chromium Project is the largest open source project on the planet. To put the sheer scale of this challenge into perspective, Chrome has more than 2,300 third-party dependencies across Chromium and satellite projects like the V8 JavaScript engine, the BoringSSL cryptography library, and foundational graphics components like Skia, ANGLE, and Dawn. About 1,700 of those are shipped to users in some capacity, woven into a wide spectrum of products from Android devices to edge computing platforms and massive cloud enterprise stacks.

To keep these dependencies patched, we rely on automated vulnerability scanning pipelines. These pipelines ingest data from Google's internal feeds as well as several external monitoring feeds, including the U.S. government's National Vulnerability Database (NVD) and the open-source focused Open Source Vulnerabilities (OSV) database.

Now more than ever, relying on reactive monitoring alone can leave a dangerous risk gap. Since the best way to stay on top of vulnerabilities and their patches is to keep third-party dependencies fresh, this year, we are starting to move all Chrome third-party dependencies onto automated update pipelines that proactively roll them to their latest upstream versions. Automation always requires guardrails, so we will also be using safety signals from projects such as Google’s Open Source Security Intelligence Platform (GOSSIP) to ensure that we are accounting for other risks in the third-party open source software ecosystem.

Moving forward

While this dramatic change in software security brought about by LLMs might be startling, an increase in bugs found and fixed is not a sign of failure. Every bug found and fixed is one less foothold for an attacker. But discovering and fixing a bug is only half the battle — we must also ship the fix and apply the update for users faster than adversaries can exploit the bug, and invest in projects that mitigate or eliminate classes of bugs through accelerated release cadences, dynamic patching, and opportune restarts, we are driving toward a browser that is continuously protected without disrupting the user.

The AI era has undeniably intensified the software security threat landscape, but by combining rapid deployment mechanisms with deep structural defenses, we are ensuring the advantage remains firmly with defenders. With this, Chrome and the broader web become safer with every update.

But discovering and fixing a bug is only half the battle — we must also ship the fix and apply the update for users faster than adversaries can exploit the bug, and invest in projects that mitigate or eliminate classes of bugs through accelerated release cadences, dynamic patching, and opportune restarts, we are driving toward a browser that is continuously protected without disrupting the user.The AI era has undeniably intensified the software security threat landscape, but by combining rapid deployment mechanisms with deep structural defenses, we are ensuring the advantage remains firmly with defenders. With this, Chrome and the broader web become safer with every update.

blocks.html_en: The Chrome Security team has been using LLMs for years. In 2023 we developed ways to use LLMs to increase security fuzzing coverage and performance. In 2024, we worked with Project Zero on Naptime, giving LLMs specialized tools for vulnerability research. And in 2025, we collaborated with DeepMind and Project Zero on Big Sleep, an AI vulnerability discovery agent that successfully found bugs in the V8 JavaScript engine and graphics stack.

sentences.en: The Chrome Security team has been using LLMs for years.
sentences.zh: Chrome 安全团队多年来一直使用法学硕士。

sentences.en: In 2023 we developed ways to use LLMs to increase security fuzzing coverage and performance.
sentences.zh: 2023 年，我们开发了使用 LLM 来提高安全模糊测试覆盖率和性能的方法。

sentences.en: In 2024, we worked with Project Zero on Naptime, giving LLMs specialized tools for vulnerability research.
sentences.zh: 2024 年，我们在 Naptime 上与零项目合作，为法学硕士提供了用于漏洞研究的专用工具。

sentences.en: And in 2025, we collaborated with DeepMind and Project Zero on Big Sleep, an AI vulnerability discovery agent that successfully found bugs in the V8 JavaScript engine and graphics stack.
sentences.zh: 2025 年，我们与 DeepMind 和 Project Zero 合作开发了 Big Sleep，这是一款 AI 漏洞发现代理，成功发现了 V8 JavaScript 引擎和图形堆栈中的错误。

blocks.html_en: In early 2026, we built an agent harness that used Gemini to find vulnerabilities across the broader Chrome codebase with higher efficiency and lower false positives. One of the bugs we found was a sandbox escape that would allow a compromised renderer to trick the browser into reading local files — a bug that quietly survived in our codebase for more than 13 years! For many of us, this moment cemented the potential of AI-powered vulnerability detection.

sentences.en: In early 2026, we built an agent harness that used Gemini to find vulnerabilities across the broader Chrome codebase with higher efficiency and lower false positives.
sentences.zh: 2026 年初，我们构建了一个代理工具，使用 Gemini 在更广泛的 Chrome 代码库中查找漏洞，效率更高，误报率更低。

sentences.en: One of the bugs we found was a sandbox escape that would allow a compromised renderer to trick the browser into reading local files — a bug that quietly survived in our codebase for more than 13 years!
sentences.zh: 我们发现的错误之一是沙箱逃逸，它允许受损的渲染器欺骗浏览器读取本地文件——这个错误在我们的代码库中悄然存在了 13 年多！

sentences.en: For many of us, this moment cemented the potential of AI-powered vulnerability detection.
sentences.zh: 对于我们许多人来说，这一刻巩固了人工智能驱动的漏洞检测的潜力。

blocks.html_en: From there, we improved on our vulnerability finding agent harness by:

sentences.en: From there, we improved on our vulnerability finding agent harness by:
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我们通过以下方式改进了漏洞查找代理工具：

blocks.html_en: • Adding support for model interoperability to leverage the unique strengths of both open-weights and proprietary models.

sentences.en: Adding support for model interoperability to leverage the unique strengths of both open-weights and proprietary models.
sentences.zh: 添加对模型互操作性的支持，以利用开放权重和专有模型的独特优势。

blocks.html_en: • Building a knowledge base of Chrome, including all previously identified CVEs and Chrome’s entire Git history, to extend the LLMs reasoning capacity past its training data.

sentences.en: Building a knowledge base of Chrome, including all previously identified CVEs and Chrome’s entire Git history, to extend the LLMs reasoning capacity past its training data.
sentences.zh: 构建 Chrome 知识库，包括所有先前识别的 CVE 和 Chrome 的整个 Git 历史记录，以将 LLM 的推理能力扩展到其训练数据之外。

blocks.html_en: • Encouraging developers to add SECURITY.md files, which help models better understand trust boundaries and develop an accurate view of the threat model.

sentences.en: Encouraging developers to add SECURITY.md files, which help models better understand trust boundaries and develop an accurate view of the threat model.
sentences.zh: 鼓励开发人员添加 SECURITY.md 文件，这有助于模型更好地理解信任边界并开发威胁模型的准确视图。

blocks.html_en: • Adding a “critic” agent with a separate context to consume these SECURITY.md files.

sentences.en: Adding a “critic” agent with a separate context to consume these SECURITY.md files.
sentences.zh: 添加具有单独上下文的“批评家”代理来使用这些 SECURITY.md 文件。

blocks.html_en: • Introducing the ability to run vulnerability finding models over the codebase multiple times to account for model non-determinism and model improvements over time.

sentences.en: Introducing the ability to run vulnerability finding models over the codebase multiple times to account for model non-determinism and model improvements over time.
sentences.zh: 引入在代码库上多次运行漏洞查找模型的功能，以解决模型的不确定性和模型随时间的改进。

blocks.html_en: We’ve built all of this with safety in mind, and have put in place guardrails to mitigate the risk of AI behaving unexpectedly. Our AI analyzes source code strictly at rest, operating on locked-down machines that lack general internet access. We also utilize a dedicated setup for these internal scans that intercepts all network requests, employing strict allowlists based on the initiating application and destination, blocking any suspicious model activity. Furthermore, we never run models in an unrestricted mode, and we strictly limit our subagents from modifying the local system or accessing files outside of designated source code directories.

sentences.en: We’ve built all of this with safety in mind, and have put in place guardrails to mitigate the risk of AI behaving unexpectedly.
sentences.zh: 我们在构建所有这些时都考虑到了安全性，并设置了防护栏来降低人工智能意外行为的风险。

sentences.en: Our AI analyzes source code strictly at rest, operating on locked-down machines that lack general internet access.
sentences.zh: 我们的人工智能严格分析静态源代码，在缺乏一般互联网访问的锁定机器上运行。

sentences.en: We also utilize a dedicated setup for these internal scans that intercepts all network requests, employing strict allowlists based on the initiating application and destination, blocking any suspicious model activity.
sentences.zh: 我们还为这些内部扫描使用专用设置，拦截所有网络请求，根据启动应用程序和目的地采用严格的允许列表，阻止任何可疑的模型活动。

sentences.en: Furthermore, we never run models in an unrestricted mode, and we strictly limit our subagents from modifying the local system or accessing files outside of designated source code directories.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们从不以不受限制的模式运行模型，并且严格限制子代理修改本地系统或访问指定源代码目录之外的文件。

blocks.html_en: AI-powered vulnerability detection complements our existing security testing infrastructure. For example, fuzzing continues to be especially effective at finding bugs that arise from long-range interactions between disparate parts of our codebase, or those requiring a combination of seemingly unrelated operations.

sentences.en: AI-powered vulnerability detection complements our existing security testing infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 人工智能驱动的漏洞检测补充了我们现有的安全测试基础设施。

sentences.en: For example, fuzzing continues to be especially effective at finding bugs that arise from long-range interactions between disparate parts of our codebase, or those requiring a combination of seemingly unrelated operations.
sentences.zh: 例如，模糊测试在查找代码库不同部分之间的远程交互或需要看似不相关的操作组合的错误时仍然特别有效。

blocks.html_en: We also want to continue to reward external researchers for their expertise and creativity in finding the most challenging and impactful vulnerabilities via the Chrome Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP). In early 2026, we saw a gradual increase in all categories of bug reports, but by March, the shift was apparent: we received more bug reports than we had in the entirety of 2025. This led us to change our VRP to focus researchers on bug submissions that are additive to what we are finding internally, and easily ingestible by our newly automated processing pipelines.

sentences.en: We also want to continue to reward external researchers for their expertise and creativity in finding the most challenging and impactful vulnerabilities via the Chrome Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP).
sentences.zh: 我们还希望通过 Chrome 漏洞奖励计划 (VRP) 继续奖励外部研究人员在寻找最具挑战性和影响力的漏洞方面的专业知识和创造力。

sentences.en: In early 2026, we saw a gradual increase in all categories of bug reports, but by March, the shift was apparent: we received more bug reports than we had in the entirety of 2025.

sentences.en: This led us to change our VRP to focus researchers on bug submissions that are additive to what we are finding internally, and easily ingestible by our newly automated processing pipelines.
sentences.zh: 这导致我们改变了 VRP，将研究人员的注意力集中在 bug 提交上，这些 bug 提交是我们内部发现的内容的补充，并且可以通过我们新的自动化处理管道轻松获取。

blocks.html_en: Triaging vulnerabilities

sentences.en: Triaging vulnerabilities
sentences.zh: 对漏洞进行分类

blocks.html_en: As we discover more security vulnerabilities with AI-powered tools, we’ve simultaneously used AI to scale and automate validating, triaging, and fixing bugs. Historically, triaging a single security report took anywhere from 5 to 30 or more minutes, and relied primarily on human expertise. We have been increasingly shifting our triage process towards an automated approach that blends rule-based systems with AI to increase throughput and accuracy.

sentences.en: As we discover more security vulnerabilities with AI-powered tools, we’ve simultaneously used AI to scale and automate validating, triaging, and fixing bugs.
sentences.zh: 随着我们通过人工智能工具发现更多安全漏洞，我们同时使用人工智能来扩展和自动化验证、分类和修复错误。

sentences.en: Historically, triaging a single security report took anywhere from 5 to 30 or more minutes, and relied primarily on human expertise.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，对单个安全报告进行分类需要 5 到 30 分钟或更长时间，并且主要依赖于人类专业知识。

sentences.en: We have been increasingly shifting our triage process towards an automated approach that blends rule-based systems with AI to increase throughput and accuracy.
sentences.zh: 我们越来越多地将分诊流程转向自动化方法，将基于规则的系统与人工智能相结合，以提高吞吐量和准确性。

blocks.html_en: The automated triage process is broken down into four key phases:

sentences.en: The automated triage process is broken down into four key phases:
sentences.zh: 自动分类过程分为四个关键阶段：

blocks.html_en: • Filtering out the noise. The system checks if an incoming bug is spam, ensures it meets intake criteria (e.g. is not a duplicate), and verifies that it clearly describes a Chrome security vulnerability.

sentences.en: Filtering out the noise.
sentences.zh: 滤除噪音。

sentences.en: The system checks if an incoming bug is spam, ensures it meets intake criteria (e.g. is not a duplicate), and verifies that it clearly describes a Chrome security vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 系统检查传入的错误是否是垃圾邮件，确保其符合接收标准（例如不是重复的），并验证它是否清楚地描述了 Chrome 安全漏洞。

blocks.html_en: • Reproducing bugs. Next, the system checks for a proof of concept. Reproducible bugs are tested on the specific operating system and browser versions they affect. Based on this, the system attaches further details such as stack traces to the bug to help inform the fix.

sentences.en: Reproducing bugs.
sentences.zh: 重现错误。

sentences.en: Next, the system checks for a proof of concept.
sentences.zh: 接下来，系统检查概念验证。

sentences.en: Reproducible bugs are tested on the specific operating system and browser versions they affect.
sentences.zh: 可重现的错误会在其影响的特定操作系统和浏览器版本上进行测试。

sentences.en: Based on this, the system attaches further details such as stack traces to the bug to help inform the fix.
sentences.zh: 基于此，系统会将更多详细信息（例如堆栈跟踪）附加到错误中，以帮助通知修复。

blocks.html_en: • Enriching the report with metadata. The system adds essential metadata to the report, such as when the bug was first introduced and its severity rating. To help this process scale, we’ve made our severity guidelines clearer and easier to apply automatically. We continue to allow developers to modify the severity rating if they believe it is incorrect, and to add context to help models reason about security boundaries using SECURITY.md files.

sentences.en: Enriching the report with metadata.
sentences.zh: 使用元数据丰富报告。

sentences.en: The system adds essential metadata to the report, such as when the bug was first introduced and its severity rating.
sentences.zh: 系统将重要的元数据添加到报告中，例如首次引入错误的时间及其严重程度评级。

sentences.en: To help this process scale, we’ve made our severity guidelines clearer and easier to apply automatically.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助扩展此流程，我们使严重性准则更加清晰且更易于自动应用。

sentences.en: We continue to allow developers to modify the severity rating if they believe it is incorrect, and to add context to help models reason about security boundaries using SECURITY.md files.
sentences.zh: 我们继续允许开发人员修改严重性评级（如果他们认为严重性评级不正确），并添加上下文以帮助模型使用 SECURITY.md 文件推理安全边界。

blocks.html_en: • Automatic assigning. The system automatically routes the issue to the correct component and human owner.

sentences.en: Automatic assigning.
sentences.zh: 自动分配。

sentences.en: The system automatically routes the issue to the correct component and human owner.
sentences.zh: 系统会自动将问题发送给正确的组件和负责人。

blocks.html_en: While it's hard to measure precisely, we estimate that this new process is saving hundreds of hours of developer time per month, allowing our team to focus on other security priorities.

sentences.en: While it's hard to measure precisely, we estimate that this new process is saving hundreds of hours of developer time per month, allowing our team to focus on other security priorities.
sentences.zh: 虽然很难精确衡量，但我们估计这个新流程每月可以节省开发人员数百小时的时间，使我们的团队能够专注于其他安全优先事项。

blocks.html_en: Fixing vulnerabilities

sentences.en: Fixing vulnerabilities
sentences.zh: 修复漏洞

blocks.html_en: Across Google, developers share the responsibility of prioritizing security fixes with the security team, but scaling bug discovery requires an equally scalable bug fixing process.

sentences.en: Across Google, developers share the responsibility of prioritizing security fixes with the security team, but scaling bug discovery requires an equally scalable bug fixing process.
sentences.zh: 在整个 Google 中，开发人员与安全团队共同承担优先考虑安全修复的责任，但扩展错误发现需要同样可扩展的错误修复流程。

blocks.html_en: To achieve this, we rely on multi-agent workflows throughout:

sentences.en: To achieve this, we rely on multi-agent workflows throughout:
sentences.zh: 为了实现这一目标，我们始终依赖多代理工作流程：

blocks.html_en: • After initial build steps that bring in context from a specific issue, we run a fixing agent that returns multiple candidate fixes.

sentences.en: After initial build steps that bring in context from a specific issue, we run a fixing agent that returns multiple candidate fixes.
sentences.zh: 在引入特定问题上下文的初始构建步骤之后，我们运行一个修复代理，该代理返回多个候选修复。

blocks.html_en: • A critic agent then evaluates which would be the best fit, producing other relevant artifacts for developers to evaluate the fix.

sentences.en: A critic agent then evaluates which would be the best fit, producing other relevant artifacts for developers to evaluate the fix.
sentences.zh: 然后，评论家代理会评估哪一个最适合，并为开发人员生成其他相关工件来评估修复。

blocks.html_en: • The fixing and critic agents work in a loop that mimics a typical code review process to ensure that code is functional and compliant with Chromium and Google style guidelines, as well as other local code conventions.

sentences.en: The fixing and critic agents work in a loop that mimics a typical code review process to ensure that code is functional and compliant with Chromium and Google style guidelines, as well as other local code conventions.
sentences.zh: 修复和批评代理在一个循环中工作，模仿典型的代码审查过程，以确保代码功能正常并符合 Chromium 和 Google 风格指南以及其他本地代码约定。

blocks.html_en: • Test-writing agents help write tests for fixes. These agents can ensure that tests work across the full array of Chrome supported platforms and configurations before a developer reviews the fix, saving up to weeks of developer time.

sentences.en: Test-writing agents help write tests for fixes.
sentences.zh: 测试编写代理帮助编写修复测试。

sentences.en: These agents can ensure that tests work across the full array of Chrome supported platforms and configurations before a developer reviews the fix, saving up to weeks of developer time.
sentences.zh: 这些代理可以确保在开发人员查看修复之前，测试可以在所有 Chrome 支持的平台和配置上进行，从而节省长达数周的开发时间。

sentences.en: Number of security bugs fixed in recent Chrome Stable release milestones

blocks.html_en: Once a fix has landed and is visible in the public open source codebase, attackers can start to reverse engineer and exploit the bug before the fix reaches users’ machines — so called "N-day" attacks. This is commonly referred to as the “patch gap.” Since fixes committed to the main “tree” typically take weeks to reach the Chrome Stable channel (what the vast majority of our users run), minimizing this patch gap is a critical part of our strategy.

sentences.en: Once a fix has landed and is visible in the public open source codebase, attackers can start to reverse engineer and exploit the bug before the fix reaches users’ machines — so called "N-day" attacks.
sentences.zh: 一旦修复程序发布并在公共开源代码库中可见，攻击者就可以在修复程序到达用户计算机之前开始逆向工程并利用该错误，即所谓的“N 天”攻击。

sentences.en: This is commonly referred to as the “patch gap.”
sentences.zh: 这通常称为“补丁间隙”。

sentences.en: Since fixes committed to the main “tree” typically take weeks to reach the Chrome Stable channel (what the vast majority of our users run), minimizing this patch gap is a critical part of our strategy.
sentences.zh: 由于针对主“树”的修复通常需要数周时间才能到达 Chrome 稳定版渠道（我们绝大多数用户运行的渠道），因此最大限度地减少补丁间隙是我们策略的关键部分。

blocks.html_en: Based on their severity, security fixes are merged directly from the main “tree” into the active Chrome stable release branch, which is continuously monitored to prevent new crashes or regressions. We are in the process of transitioning to a two-week cadence for major Chrome milestones, with weekly security updates. However, in the face of fast-moving, AI-powered attacks, our delivery cadence must accelerate even further. To meet this moment, we are piloting a shift to two security releases per week.

sentences.en: Based on their severity, security fixes are merged directly from the main “tree” into the active Chrome stable release branch, which is continuously monitored to prevent new crashes or regressions.
sentences.zh: 根据其严重性，安全修复程序会直接从主“树”合并到活动的 Chrome 稳定版本分支中，该分支会受到持续监控，以防止新的崩溃或回归。

sentences.en: We are in the process of transitioning to a two-week cadence for major Chrome milestones, with weekly security updates.
sentences.zh: 我们正在将主要 Chrome 里程碑的节奏转变为每两周一次，并每周进行安全更新。

sentences.en: However, in the face of fast-moving, AI-powered attacks, our delivery cadence must accelerate even further.
sentences.zh: 然而，面对快速移动的人工智能攻击，我们的交付节奏必须进一步加快。

sentences.en: To meet this moment, we are piloting a shift to two security releases per week.
sentences.zh: 为了迎接这一时刻，我们正在尝试每周发布两次安全版本。

blocks.html_en: Even with this pace, proper public disclosure remains paramount. Every security bug that reaches Chrome Stable, regardless of whether it was discovered internally or reported externally, is documented and disclosed publicly as a standard best practice. We are working on automating the generation of release notes and CVE descriptions from security bug fixes to eliminate manual bottlenecks and shorten the window between vulnerability discovery and public disclosure.

sentences.en: Even with this pace, proper public disclosure remains paramount.
sentences.zh: 即使按照这样的速度，适当的公开披露仍然至关重要。

sentences.en: Every security bug that reaches Chrome Stable, regardless of whether it was discovered internally or reported externally, is documented and disclosed publicly as a standard best practice.
sentences.zh: Chrome 稳定版的每个安全漏洞，无论是内部发现的还是外部报告的，都会作为标准最佳实践进行记录和公开披露。

sentences.en: We are working on automating the generation of release notes and CVE descriptions from security bug fixes to eliminate manual bottlenecks and shorten the window between vulnerability discovery and public disclosure.
sentences.zh: 我们正在致力于从安全错误修复中自动生成发行说明和 CVE 描述，以消除手动瓶颈并缩短漏洞发现和公开披露之间的窗口。

blocks.html_en: Applying updates

sentences.en: Applying updates
sentences.zh: 应用更新

blocks.html_en: In 2008, Chrome pioneered the concept of silent, background software updates: new binaries are automatically downloaded and staged on disk with minimal user intervention. At the next restart of the browser, the update would be applied and the user would be protected. However, compared to the 1–2 days it takes for triage, fix, test and release, the time spent waiting for the user to restart Chrome can be a significant contributor to N-day exploitation risk.

sentences.en: In 2008, Chrome pioneered the concept of silent, background software updates: new binaries are automatically downloaded and staged on disk with minimal user intervention.
sentences.zh: 2008 年，Chrome 首创了静默后台软件更新的概念：新的二进制文件会自动下载并暂存在磁盘上，只需最少的用户干预。

sentences.en: At the next restart of the browser, the update would be applied and the user would be protected.
sentences.zh: 下次重新启动浏览器时，将应用更新并保护用户。

sentences.en: However, compared to the 1–2 days it takes for triage, fix, test and release, the time spent waiting for the user to restart Chrome can be a significant contributor to N-day exploitation risk.
sentences.zh: 然而，与分类、修复、测试和发布所需的 1-2 天时间相比，等待用户重新启动 Chrome 所花费的时间可能是 N 天利用风险的一个重要因素。

blocks.html_en: People have understandable reasons to delay restarting Chrome. A restart can be disruptive, requires scheduling in-between tasks, and is rarely the top priority at any given moment. To eliminate this friction, we are pioneering ways to shift the burden away from the user by:

sentences.en: People have understandable reasons to delay restarting Chrome.
sentences.zh: 人们有可以理解的理由推迟重启 Chrome。

sentences.en: A restart can be disruptive, requires scheduling in-between tasks, and is rarely the top priority at any given moment.
sentences.zh: 重新启动可能会造成破坏，需要在任务之间进行调度，并且在任何给定时刻都很少是重中之重。

sentences.en: To eliminate this friction, we are pioneering ways to shift the burden away from the user by:
sentences.zh: 为了消除这种摩擦，我们正在开创性地通过以下方式减轻用户的负担：

blocks.html_en: • Investing in "dynamic patching" that will eliminate the need for a full browser restart in most cases. By leveraging Chrome’s multi-process architecture, dynamic patching sequentially replaces background child processes (like the Renderer and GPU) with updated binaries on the fly. Stay tuned to learn more as we research and develop this feature.

sentences.en: Investing in "dynamic patching" that will eliminate the need for a full browser restart in most cases.
sentences.zh: 投资“动态修补”将消除在大多数情况下完全重新启动浏览器的需要。

sentences.en: By leveraging Chrome’s multi-process architecture, dynamic patching sequentially replaces background child processes (like the Renderer and GPU) with updated binaries on the fly.
sentences.zh: 通过利用 Chrome 的多进程架构，动态修补会按顺序用动态更新的二进制文件替换后台子进程（例如渲染器和 GPU）。

sentences.en: Stay tuned to learn more as we research and develop this feature.
sentences.zh: 请继续关注我们研究和开发此功能以了解更多信息。

blocks.html_en: • Exploring ways to ensure a seamless session restore even in complex cases, by saving more state locally.

sentences.en: Exploring ways to ensure a seamless session restore even in complex cases, by saving more state locally.
sentences.zh: 通过在本地保存更多状态，探索即使在复杂情况下也能确保无缝会话恢复的方法。

blocks.html_en: • Finding opportune moments to restart automatically, when we can guarantee a seamless session restore. For example, in Chrome 150, we rolled out a change to take advantage of the unique application state on macOS where applications typically continue running in the background even after all windows are closed. Now, if Chrome detects a pending update while in this windowless state, it automatically restarts.

sentences.en: Finding opportune moments to restart automatically, when we can guarantee a seamless session restore.
sentences.zh: 寻找合适的时机自动重新启动，此时我们可以保证无缝会话恢复。

sentences.en: For example, in Chrome 150, we rolled out a change to take advantage of the unique application state on macOS where applications typically continue running in the background even after all windows are closed.
sentences.zh: 例如，在 Chrome 150 中，我们进行了一项更改，以利用 macOS 上独特的应用程序状态，即使所有窗口关闭后，应用程序通常也会在后台继续运行。

sentences.en: Now, if Chrome detects a pending update while in this windowless state, it automatically restarts.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果 Chrome 在这种无窗口状态下检测到挂起的更新，它会自动重新启动。

blocks.html_en: Zero window auto-restart on macOS

sentences.en: Zero window auto-restart on macOS
sentences.zh: macOS 上的零窗口自动重启

blocks.html_en: Our long-term vision is a browser that is always up-to-date – continuously and dynamically patched, and automatically restarted during opportune periods of minimal disruption. While we’re working on this, you can keep your Chrome up to date by clicking on the update message in the top right corner.

sentences.en: Our long-term vision is a browser that is always up-to-date – continuously and dynamically patched, and automatically restarted during opportune periods of minimal disruption.
sentences.zh: 我们的长期愿景是打造一款始终保持最新状态的浏览器——持续动态修补，并在干扰最小的适当时期自动重新启动。

sentences.en: While we’re working on this, you can keep your Chrome up to date by clicking on the update message in the top right corner.
sentences.zh: 在我们解决此问题期间，您可以通过点击右上角的更新消息来使 Chrome 保持最新状态。

blocks.html_en: For enterprise customers looking to keep Chrome up to date, we recommend that IT admins:

sentences.en: For enterprise customers looking to keep Chrome up to date, we recommend that IT admins:
sentences.zh: 对于希望使 Chrome 保持最新状态的企业客户，我们建议 IT 管理员：

blocks.html_en: • Apply the RelaunchNotification policy which prompts users to restart Chrome to apply a pending update, escalating from a gentle reminder to a forced restart over a set timeframe.

sentences.en: Apply the RelaunchNotification policy which prompts users to restart Chrome to apply a pending update, escalating from a gentle reminder to a forced restart over a set timeframe.
sentences.zh: 应用 RelaunchNotification 政策，提示用户重新启动 Chrome 以应用待处理的更新，从温和提醒升级为在设定时间范围内强制重新启动。

blocks.html_en: • Utilize the Chrome Extended Stable Channel for highly sensitive environments where software changes must be vetted.

sentences.en: Utilize the Chrome Extended Stable Channel for highly sensitive environments where software changes must be vetted.
sentences.zh: 将 Chrome 扩展稳定通道用于必须审查软件更改的高度敏感环境。

blocks.html_en: • Leverage the OS-agnostic dashboard provided by Chrome Enterprise Core or Premium to track fleet-wide browser versions and manage updates at a more granular level.

sentences.en: Leverage the OS-agnostic dashboard provided by Chrome Enterprise Core or Premium to track fleet-wide browser versions and manage updates at a more granular level.
sentences.zh: 利用 Chrome Enterprise Core 或 Premium 提供的与操作系统无关的仪表板来跟踪整个舰队的浏览器版本并更精细地管理更新。

blocks.html_en: Prevention is better than cure

sentences.en: Prevention is better than cure
sentences.zh: 预防胜于治疗

blocks.html_en: Beyond fixing individual security bugs, we’re also investing in the mitigation and elimination of entire classes of security bugs, as well as in preventing them from landing in the first place. With AI coding advancements, we believe there are exciting opportunities to accelerate projects that would have previously taken years, or never happened.

sentences.en: Beyond fixing individual security bugs, we’re also investing in the mitigation and elimination of entire classes of security bugs, as well as in preventing them from landing in the first place.
sentences.zh: 除了修复个别安全错误之外，我们还投资于缓解和消除整类安全错误，并从一开始就防止它们出现。

sentences.en: With AI coding advancements, we believe there are exciting opportunities to accelerate projects that would have previously taken years, or never happened.
sentences.zh: 随着人工智能编码的进步，我们相信有令人兴奋的机会来加速以前需要数年时间或从未发生过的项目。

blocks.html_en: Memory safety mitigations

sentences.en: Memory safety mitigations
sentences.zh: 内存安全缓解措施

blocks.html_en: Chrome is executing on a two-layered memory safety strategy: hardening our runtime environment to neutralize legacy C++ vulnerabilities, while shifting to memory-safe languages for long-term architectural resilience.

sentences.en: Chrome is executing on a two-layered memory safety strategy: hardening our runtime environment to neutralize legacy C++ vulnerabilities, while shifting to memory-safe languages for long-term architectural resilience.
sentences.zh: Chrome 正在执行两层内存安全策略：强化我们的运行时环境以消除遗留的 C++ 漏洞，同时转向内存安全语言以实现长期架构弹性。

blocks.html_en: The vast majority of the Chromium codebase remains in C++, making immediate toolchain and runtime mitigations our critical first line of defense. We have long prioritized memory-safety engineering at scale, deploying hardened standard template libraries and pioneering technologies like the MiraclePtr family to neutralize Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerabilities. AI-powered vulnerability detection only reaffirms the need for such technology.

sentences.en: The vast majority of the Chromium codebase remains in C++, making immediate toolchain and runtime mitigations our critical first line of defense.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数 Chromium 代码库仍然采用 C++，这使得即时工具链和运行时缓解措施成为我们关键的第一道防线。

sentences.en: We have long prioritized memory-safety engineering at scale, deploying hardened standard template libraries and pioneering technologies like the MiraclePtr family to neutralize Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerabilities.
sentences.zh: 我们长期以来一直优先考虑大规模内存安全工程，部署强化的标准模板库和 MiraclePtr 系列等开创性技术来消除释放后使用 (UAF) 漏洞。

sentences.en: AI-powered vulnerability detection only reaffirms the need for such technology.
sentences.zh: 人工智能驱动的漏洞检测只是重申了对此类技术的需求。

blocks.html_en: Our C++ defensive roadmap is focused on three pillars:

sentences.en: Our C++ defensive roadmap is focused on three pillars:
sentences.zh: 我们的 C++ 防御路线图重点关注三个支柱：

blocks.html_en: • MiraclePtr & MiracleObject Expansion. Having already driven a major reduction in UAF bugs via MiraclePtr, we are expanding this paradigm to more libraries such as Skia, ANGLE, Dawn, C++ iterators and std:: containers. We are also actively deploying MiracleObject with the aim of neutralizing up to 90% of UAF vulnerabilities on the GPU main thread, deliberately trading localized runtime performance for temporal safety.

sentences.en: MiraclePtr & MiracleObject Expansion.
sentences.zh: MiraclePtr 和 MiracleObject 扩展。

sentences.en: Having already driven a major reduction in UAF bugs via MiraclePtr, we are expanding this paradigm to more libraries such as Skia, ANGLE, Dawn, C++ iterators and std:: containers.
sentences.zh: 通过 MiraclePtr 已经大幅减少了 UAF 错误，我们正在将此范例扩展到更多库，例如 Skia、ANGLE、Dawn、C++ 迭代器和 std:: 容器。

sentences.en: We are also actively deploying MiracleObject with the aim of neutralizing up to 90% of UAF vulnerabilities on the GPU main thread, deliberately trading localized runtime performance for temporal safety.
sentences.zh: 我们还积极部署 MiracleObject，旨在消除 GPU 主线程上高达 90% 的 UAF 漏洞，刻意用本地化运行时性能换取时间安全。

blocks.html_en: • Spanification. To systematically eliminate Out-of-Bounds (OOB) spatial safety errors, Chrome has undertaken a massive "spanification" effort, migrating legacy pointer-and-size constructs to compiler-enforced std::span types. Currently, 97% of first-party Chrome code compiles cleanly with strict unsafe-buffer warnings. We are now pushing these requirements downstream, expanding spanification into foundational codebases like Skia, ANGLE, and Dawn.

sentences.en: Spanification.
sentences.zh: 西班牙化。

sentences.en: To systematically eliminate Out-of-Bounds (OOB) spatial safety errors, Chrome has undertaken a massive "spanification" effort, migrating legacy pointer-and-size constructs to compiler-enforced std::span types.
sentences.zh: 为了系统地消除越界 (OOB) 空间安全错误，Chrome 进行了大量的“扩展”工作，将遗留的指针和大小结构迁移到编译器强制执行的 std::span 类型。

sentences.en: Currently, 97% of first-party Chrome code compiles cleanly with strict unsafe-buffer warnings.
sentences.zh: 目前，97% 的第一方 Chrome 代码可以干净地编译，并带有严格的不安全缓冲区警告。

sentences.en: We are now pushing these requirements downstream, expanding spanification into foundational codebases like Skia, ANGLE, and Dawn.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在将这些需求推向下游，将跨度扩展至 Skia、ANGLE 和 Dawn 等基础代码库。

blocks.html_en: • Structural & Allocation Hardening. We are working on integrating checked math for calculations tied to memory allocations to block integer overflow avenues. Concurrently, Chrome is implementing an additional level of heap partitioning to strictly segregate pointer-containing types from non-pointer types to make it harder to exploit UAF bugs.

sentences.en: Structural & Allocation Hardening.
sentences.zh: 结构和分配强化。

sentences.en: We are working on integrating checked math for calculations tied to memory allocations to block integer overflow avenues.
sentences.zh: 我们正在致力于集成与内存分配相关的计算检查数学，以阻止整数溢出途径。

sentences.en: Concurrently, Chrome is implementing an additional level of heap partitioning to strictly segregate pointer-containing types from non-pointer types to make it harder to exploit UAF bugs.
sentences.zh: 同时，Chrome 正在实现额外级别的堆分区，以严格将包含指针的类型与非指针类型分开，从而更难利用 UAF 错误。

blocks.html_en: While C++ safety enhancements provide an immediate shield, we believe that runtime mitigations will hit diminishing marginal returns within the next few years. Runtime checks are inherently more expensive than compile-time guarantees, and even a heavily mitigated C++ binary requires rigid, performance-throttling sandboxing to comply with the Rule of Two.

sentences.en: While C++ safety enhancements provide an immediate shield, we believe that runtime mitigations will hit diminishing marginal returns within the next few years.
sentences.zh: 虽然 C++ 安全增强功能提供了立竿见影的保护，但我们相信运行时缓解措施将在未来几年内实现边际收益递减。

sentences.en: Runtime checks are inherently more expensive than compile-time guarantees, and even a heavily mitigated C++ binary requires rigid, performance-throttling sandboxing to comply with the Rule of Two.
sentences.zh: 运行时检查本质上比编译时保证更昂贵，即使是经过严格缓解的 C++ 二进制文件也需要严格的性能限制沙箱来遵守“二法则”。

blocks.html_en: The long-term solution is shifting the codebase towards memory-safe languages like Rust, focusing on the following core tenets:

sentences.en: The long-term solution is shifting the codebase towards memory-safe languages like Rust, focusing on the following core tenets:
sentences.zh: 长期解决方案是将代码库转向 Rust 等内存安全语言，重点关注以下核心原则：

blocks.html_en: • Rust flywheel. Developers cannot be expected to entirely absorb the velocity friction of engineering in a new language ecosystem. As such, we are building a centralized Rust SDK that exposes foundational Chromium APIs and tooling directly to Rust. Our aim is to turn Rust into a routine, frictionless engineering choice for new components.

sentences.en: Rust flywheel.
sentences.zh: 飞轮生锈。

sentences.en: Developers cannot be expected to entirely absorb the velocity friction of engineering in a new language ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 不能指望开发人员完全吸收新语言生态系统中工程的速度摩擦。

sentences.en: As such, we are building a centralized Rust SDK that exposes foundational Chromium APIs and tooling directly to Rust.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们正在构建一个集中式 Rust SDK，直接向 Rust 公开基础 Chromium API 和工具。

sentences.en: Our aim is to turn Rust into a routine, frictionless engineering choice for new components.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是将 Rust 变成新组件的常规、无摩擦工程选择。

blocks.html_en: • Targeted “bug nest” eradication. Rust is being deployed strategically to replace code segments that exhibit high historical bug density (such as complex data parsers, image codecs, and font stacks).

sentences.en: Targeted “bug nest” eradication.
sentences.zh: 有针对性地消灭“虫巢”。

sentences.en: Rust is being deployed strategically to replace code segments that exhibit high historical bug density (such as complex data parsers, image codecs, and font stacks).
sentences.zh: Rust 正在战略性地部署，以替换具有高历史错误密度的代码段（例如复杂的数据解析器、图像编解码器和字体堆栈）。

blocks.html_en: • Enabling high-privilege modularization. By writing new modular components in Rust, Chrome can safely execute complex features inside high-privilege processes (like the browser process) without the performance penalties of sandboxing, breaking the constraints of traditional C++ architecture.

sentences.en: Enabling high-privilege modularization.
sentences.zh: 实现高权限模块化。

sentences.en: By writing new modular components in Rust, Chrome can safely execute complex features inside high-privilege processes (like the browser process) without the performance penalties of sandboxing, breaking the constraints of traditional C++ architecture.
sentences.zh: 通过用 Rust 编写新的模块化组件，Chrome 可以在高权限进程（如浏览器进程）内安全地执行复杂功能，而不会受到沙箱性能的影响，从而打破了传统 C++ 架构的限制。

blocks.html_en: In addition to Rust, we are also exploring options like implementing the browser’s top-level user interface using HTML, CSS, and TypeScript to further reduce dependencies on traditional C++ frameworks.

sentences.en: In addition to Rust, we are also exploring options like implementing the browser’s top-level user interface using HTML, CSS, and TypeScript to further reduce dependencies on traditional C++ frameworks.
sentences.zh: 除了 Rust 之外，我们还在探索使用 HTML、CSS 和 TypeScript 实现浏览器的顶级用户界面等选项，以进一步减少对传统 C++ 框架的依赖。

blocks.html_en: Catching security bugs before they land

sentences.en: Catching security bugs before they land
sentences.zh: 在安全漏洞落地之前发现它们

blocks.html_en: Bulk scanning of a code base cannot keep pace with Chrome’s high-traffic development velocity. To account for this, we’re also deploying AI-powered bug-finding capabilities to identify and prevent bugs as close to code submit-time as possible. Part of Chrome’s continuous integration (CI) and commit queue (CQ) pipeline, these defensive models automatically scan diffs to prevent new vulnerabilities by performing actions like suggesting spanification fixes, flagging dangling pointers, and enforcing numeric safety.

sentences.en: Bulk scanning of a code base cannot keep pace with Chrome’s high-traffic development velocity.
sentences.zh: 对代码库的批量扫描无法跟上 Chrome 高流量的开发速度。

sentences.en: To account for this, we’re also deploying AI-powered bug-finding capabilities to identify and prevent bugs as close to code submit-time as possible.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这一点，我们还部署了人工智能驱动的错误查找功能，以尽可能在代码提交时间附近识别和防止错误。

sentences.en: Part of Chrome’s continuous integration (CI) and commit queue (CQ) pipeline, these defensive models automatically scan diffs to prevent new vulnerabilities by performing actions like suggesting spanification fixes, flagging dangling pointers, and enforcing numeric safety.
sentences.zh: 作为 Chrome 持续集成 (CI) 和提交队列 (CQ) 管道的一部分，这些防御模型会自动扫描差异，通过执行建议跨度修复、标记悬空指针和强制数字安全等操作来防止新漏洞。

blocks.html_en: Additionally, a major challenge in large-scale software engineering is the “latent security issue.” Code that is safe and robust in isolation can be transformed into a critical vulnerability by an entirely unrelated, minor logic change elsewhere in the tree. By utilizing continuous, LLM-powered semantic analysis within the CQ, Chrome can intercept these compound risks before they land in the tree, catching the subtle or complex interactions that traditional static analysis misses.

sentences.en: Additionally, a major challenge in large-scale software engineering is the “latent security issue.”
sentences.zh: 此外，大规模软件工程的一个主要挑战是“潜在的安全问题”。

sentences.en: Code that is safe and robust in isolation can be transformed into a critical vulnerability by an entirely unrelated, minor logic change elsewhere in the tree.
sentences.zh: 孤立地安全且健壮的代码可能会因树中其他地方完全不相关的微小逻辑更改而转变为严重漏洞。

sentences.en: By utilizing continuous, LLM-powered semantic analysis within the CQ, Chrome can intercept these compound risks before they land in the tree, catching the subtle or complex interactions that traditional static analysis misses.
sentences.zh: 通过在 CQ 中利用由 LLM 支持的连续语义分析，Chrome 可以在这些复合风险登陆树之前拦截它们，捕捉传统静态分析错过的微妙或复杂的交互。

blocks.html_en: Securing the internet

sentences.en: Securing the internet
sentences.zh: 保护互联网安全

blocks.html_en: Keeping the web safe involves more than just securing Chrome. Google has been a long-standing supporter of open source projects and communities to ensure better security outcomes for all users. Most recently, Google joined others in donating $12.5M to the Alpha-Omega project in support of enabling maintainers to have access to the tools and support they will need in order to respond quickly to vulnerability reports. Google was also a founding member of the Akrites project, which aims to lower the burden on upstream maintainers by providing a centralized clearinghouse for vulnerability reports and a security incident response team.

sentences.en: Keeping the web safe involves more than just securing Chrome.
sentences.zh: 保持网络安全不仅仅涉及保护 Chrome。

sentences.en: Google has been a long-standing supporter of open source projects and communities to ensure better security outcomes for all users.

sentences.en: Most recently, Google joined others in donating $12.5M to the Alpha-Omega project in support of enabling maintainers to have access to the tools and support they will need in order to respond quickly to vulnerability reports.

sentences.en: Google was also a founding member of the Akrites project, which aims to lower the burden on upstream maintainers by providing a centralized clearinghouse for vulnerability reports and a security incident response team.

blocks.html_en: On the Chrome team, we feel this responsibility acutely — the Chromium Project is the largest open source project on the planet. About 1,700 of those are shipped to users in some capacity, woven into a wide spectrum of products from Android devices to edge computing platforms and massive cloud enterprise stacks.

But discovering and fixing a bug is only half the battle — we must also ship the fix and apply the update for users faster than adversaries can exploit the bug, and invest in projects that mitigate or eliminate classes of bugs through accelerated release cadences, dynamic patching, and opportune restarts, we are driving toward a browser that is continuously protected without disrupting the user.

Jul 30, 2026

|

Chrome 如何使用人工智能来改进漏洞发现、分类和修补。

Chrome 安全团队

我们正在经历软件安全行业的巨大转变。 大型语言模型 (LLM) 正在释放前所未有的自动漏洞发现功能，远远超出人类安全专业知识的限制，并需要新的方法来领先于攻击者。

这意味着大规模部署人工智能模型，以比以往更快的速度发现并修复数百个安全漏洞，以实现更大的弹性和全面的修复。

我们是这样做的。

虫子的一生

一些软件错误会产生安全隐患。 虽然纯粹的功能性错误可能会导致令人沮丧的 UI 冻结，但安全性错误（或漏洞）可用于构建漏洞。 漏洞允许攻击者在受害者的计算机上执行恶意操作，例如读取私人数据或在受害者不知情的情况下控制其计算机。

一旦安全错误进入代码库，其生命周期将按如下方式进行：

  • 发现错误了。
  • 该错误已被分类。
  • 该错误已修复。
  • Chrome 的新更新已发布并修复了错误。
  • Chrome 将重新启动并应用更新。

我们的目标是尽快完成这些步骤中的每一步。

寻找漏洞

Chrome 安全团队多年来一直使用法学硕士。 2023 年，我们开发了使用 LLM 来提高安全模糊测试覆盖率和性能的方法。 2024 年，我们在 Naptime 上与零项目合作，为法学硕士提供了用于漏洞研究的专用工具。 2025 年，我们与 DeepMind 和 Project Zero 合作开发了 Big Sleep，这是一款 AI 漏洞发现代理，成功发现了 V8 JavaScript 引擎和图形堆栈中的错误。

2026 年初，我们构建了一个代理工具，使用 Gemini 在更广泛的 Chrome 代码库中查找漏洞，效率更高，误报率更低。 我们发现的错误之一是沙箱逃逸，它允许受损的渲染器欺骗浏览器读取本地文件——这个错误在我们的代码库中悄然存在了 13 年多！ 对于我们许多人来说，这一刻巩固了人工智能驱动的漏洞检测的潜力。

从那时起，我们通过以下方式改进了漏洞查找代理工具：

  • 添加对模型互操作性的支持，以利用开放权重和专有模型的独特优势。
  • 构建 Chrome 知识库，包括所有先前识别的 CVE 和 Chrome 的整个 Git 历史记录，以将 LLM 的推理能力扩展到其训练数据之外。
  • 鼓励开发人员添加 SECURITY.md 文件，这有助于模型更好地理解信任边界并开发威胁模型的准确视图。
  • 添加具有单独上下文的“批评家”代理来使用这些 SECURITY.md 文件。
  • 引入在代码库上多次运行漏洞查找模型的功能，以解决模型的不确定性和模型随时间的改进。

我们在构建所有这些时都考虑到了安全性，并设置了防护栏来降低人工智能意外行为的风险。 我们的人工智能严格分析静态源代码，在缺乏一般互联网访问的锁定机器上运行。 我们还为这些内部扫描使用专用设置，拦截所有网络请求，根据启动应用程序和目的地采用严格的允许列表，阻止任何可疑的模型活动。 此外，我们从不以不受限制的模式运行模型，并且严格限制子代理修改本地系统或访问指定源代码目录之外的文件。

人工智能驱动的漏洞检测补充了我们现有的安全测试基础设施。 例如，模糊测试在查找代码库不同部分之间的远程交互或需要看似不相关的操作组合的错误时仍然特别有效。

我们还希望通过 Chrome 漏洞奖励计划 (VRP) 继续奖励外部研究人员在寻找最具挑战性和影响力的漏洞方面的专业知识和创造力。 2026 年初，我们看到所有类别的错误报告逐渐增加，但到 3 月份，这种转变很明显：我们收到的错误报告比 2025 年全年还要多。 这导致我们改变了 VRP，将研究人员的注意力集中在 bug 提交上，这些 bug 提交是我们内部发现的内容的补充，并且可以通过我们新的自动化处理管道轻松获取。

对漏洞进行分类

随着我们通过人工智能工具发现更多安全漏洞，我们同时使用人工智能来扩展和自动化验证、分类和修复错误。 从历史上看，对单个安全报告进行分类需要 5 到 30 分钟或更长时间，并且主要依赖于人类专业知识。 我们越来越多地将分诊流程转向自动化方法，将基于规则的系统与人工智能相结合，以提高吞吐量和准确性。

自动分类过程分为四个关键阶段：

  1. 滤除噪音。 系统检查传入的错误是否是垃圾邮件，确保其符合接收标准（例如不是重复的），并验证它是否清楚地描述了 Chrome 安全漏洞。
  2. 重现错误。 接下来，系统检查概念验证。 可重现的错误会在其影响的特定操作系统和浏览器版本上进行测试。 基于此，系统会将更多详细信息（例如堆栈跟踪）附加到错误中，以帮助通知修复。
  3. 使用元数据丰富报告。 系统将重要的元数据添加到报告中，例如首次引入错误的时间及其严重程度评级。 为了帮助扩展此流程，我们使严重性准则更加清晰且更易于自动应用。 我们继续允许开发人员修改严重性评级（如果他们认为严重性评级不正确），并添加上下文以帮助模型使用 SECURITY.md 文件推理安全边界。
  4. 自动分配。 系统会自动将问题发送给正确的组件和负责人。

虽然很难精确衡量，但我们估计这个新流程每月可以节省开发人员数百小时的时间，使我们的团队能够专注于其他安全优先事项。

修复漏洞

在整个 Google 中，开发人员与安全团队共同承担优先考虑安全修复的责任，但扩展错误发现需要同样可扩展的错误修复流程。

为了实现这一目标，我们始终依赖多代理工作流程：

  • 在引入特定问题上下文的初始构建步骤之后，我们运行一个修复代理，该代理返回多个候选修复。
  • 然后，评论家代理会评估哪一个最适合，并为开发人员生成其他相关工件来评估修复。
  • 修复和批评代理在一个循环中工作，模仿典型的代码审查过程，以确保代码功能正常并符合 Chromium 和 Google 风格指南以及其他本地代码约定。
  • 测试编写代理帮助编写修复测试。 这些代理可以确保在开发人员查看修复之前，测试可以在所有 Chrome 支持的平台和配置上进行，从而节省长达数周的开发时间。

此时，我们已经让法学硕士为大多数漏洞生成了候选修复程序，从而大大提高了最近 Chrome 版本中的安全修复率：

最近 Chrome 稳定版里程碑中修复的安全错误数量

在最后两个里程碑（Chrome 149 和 150）中，我们修复了 1072 个安全错误，超过了之前 23 个里程碑修复的安全错误总数。

我们与 Google DeepMind 和 Project Zero 密切合作多年，包括在 BigSleep 和 CodeMender 方面。 这些工具原生集成到我们的持续集成 (CI) 系统中，在所有 CL 中每 24 小时运行一次，以主动检测安全错误。 这种集成取得了重大成果：仅在 5 月份，我们就阻止了 20 多个漏洞进入生产环境，其中包括一个关键的 S1+ 问题。

发布修复

一旦修复程序发布并在公共开源代码库中可见，攻击者就可以在修复程序到达用户计算机之前开始逆向工程并利用该错误，即所谓的“N 天”攻击。 这通常称为“补丁间隙”。 由于针对主“树”的修复通常需要数周时间才能到达 Chrome 稳定版渠道（我们绝大多数用户运行的渠道），因此最大限度地减少补丁间隙是我们策略的关键部分。

根据其严重性，安全修复程序会直接从主“树”合并到活动的 Chrome 稳定版本分支中，该分支会受到持续监控，以防止新的崩溃或回归。 我们正在将主要 Chrome 里程碑的节奏转变为每两周一次，并每周进行安全更新。 然而，面对快速移动的人工智能攻击，我们的交付节奏必须进一步加快。 为了迎接这一时刻，我们正在尝试每周发布两次安全版本。

即使按照这样的速度，适当的公开披露仍然至关重要。 Chrome 稳定版的每个安全漏洞，无论是内部发现的还是外部报告的，都会作为标准最佳实践进行记录和公开披露。 我们正在致力于从安全错误修复中自动生成发行说明和 CVE 描述，以消除手动瓶颈并缩短漏洞发现和公开披露之间的窗口。

应用更新

2008 年，Chrome 首创了静默后台软件更新的概念：新的二进制文件会自动下载并暂存在磁盘上，只需最少的用户干预。 下次重新启动浏览器时，将应用更新并保护用户。 然而，与分类、修复、测试和发布所需的 1-2 天时间相比，等待用户重新启动 Chrome 所花费的时间可能是 N 天利用风险的一个重要因素。

人们有可以理解的理由推迟重启 Chrome。 重新启动可能会造成破坏，需要在任务之间进行调度，并且在任何给定时刻都很少是重中之重。 为了消除这种摩擦，我们正在开创性地通过以下方式减轻用户的负担：

  • 投资“动态修补”将消除在大多数情况下完全重新启动浏览器的需要。 通过利用 Chrome 的多进程架构，动态修补会按顺序用动态更新的二进制文件替换后台子进程（例如渲染器和 GPU）。 请继续关注我们研究和开发此功能以了解更多信息。
  • 通过在本地保存更多状态，探索即使在复杂情况下也能确保无缝会话恢复的方法。
  • 寻找合适的时机自动重新启动，此时我们可以保证无缝会话恢复。 例如，在 Chrome 150 中，我们进行了一项更改，以利用 macOS 上独特的应用程序状态，即使所有窗口关闭后，应用程序通常也会在后台继续运行。 现在，如果 Chrome 在这种无窗口状态下检测到挂起的更新，它会自动重新启动。

macOS 上的零窗口自动重启

我们的长期愿景是打造一款始终保持最新状态的浏览器——持续动态修补，并在干扰最小的适当时期自动重新启动。 在我们解决此问题期间，您可以通过点击右上角的更新消息来使 Chrome 保持最新状态。

对于希望使 Chrome 保持最新状态的企业客户，我们建议 IT 管理员：

  • 应用 RelaunchNotification 政策，提示用户重新启动 Chrome 以应用待处理的更新，从温和提醒升级为在设定时间范围内强制重新启动。
  • 将 Chrome 扩展稳定通道用于必须审查软件更改的高度敏感环境。
  • 利用 Chrome Enterprise Core 或 Premium 提供的与操作系统无关的仪表板来跟踪整个舰队的浏览器版本并更精细地管理更新。

预防胜于治疗

除了修复个别安全错误之外，我们还投资于缓解和消除整类安全错误，并从一开始就防止它们出现。 随着人工智能编码的进步，我们相信有令人兴奋的机会来加速以前需要数年时间或从未发生过的项目。

内存安全缓解措施

Chrome 正在执行两层内存安全策略：强化我们的运行时环境以消除遗留的 C++ 漏洞，同时转向内存安全语言以实现长期架构弹性。

绝大多数 Chromium 代码库仍然采用 C++，这使得即时工具链和运行时缓解措施成为我们关键的第一道防线。 我们长期以来一直优先考虑大规模内存安全工程，部署强化的标准模板库和 MiraclePtr 系列等开创性技术来消除释放后使用 (UAF) 漏洞。 人工智能驱动的漏洞检测只是重申了对此类技术的需求。

我们的 C++ 防御路线图重点关注三个支柱：

  • MiraclePtr 和 MiracleObject 扩展。 通过 MiraclePtr 已经大幅减少了 UAF 错误，我们正在将此范例扩展到更多库，例如 Skia、ANGLE、Dawn、C++ 迭代器和 std:: 容器。 我们还积极部署 MiracleObject，旨在消除 GPU 主线程上高达 90% 的 UAF 漏洞，刻意用本地化运行时性能换取时间安全。
  • 西班牙化。 为了系统地消除越界 (OOB) 空间安全错误，Chrome 进行了大量的“扩展”工作，将遗留的指针和大小结构迁移到编译器强制执行的 std::span 类型。 目前，97% 的第一方 Chrome 代码可以干净地编译，并带有严格的不安全缓冲区警告。 我们现在正在将这些需求推向下游，将跨度扩展至 Skia、ANGLE 和 Dawn 等基础代码库。
  • 结构和分配强化。 我们正在致力于集成与内存分配相关的计算检查数学，以阻止整数溢出途径。 同时，Chrome 正在实现额外级别的堆分区，以严格将包含指针的类型与非指针类型分开，从而更难利用 UAF 错误。

虽然 C++ 安全增强功能提供了立竿见影的保护，但我们相信运行时缓解措施将在未来几年内实现边际收益递减。 运行时检查本质上比编译时保证更昂贵，即使是经过严格缓解的 C++ 二进制文件也需要严格的性能限制沙箱来遵守“二法则”。

长期解决方案是将代码库转向 Rust 等内存安全语言，重点关注以下核心原则：

  • 飞轮生锈。 不能指望开发人员完全吸收新语言生态系统中工程的速度摩擦。 因此，我们正在构建一个集中式 Rust SDK，直接向 Rust 公开基础 Chromium API 和工具。 我们的目标是将 Rust 变成新组件的常规、无摩擦工程选择。
  • 有针对性地消灭“虫巢”。 Rust 正在战略性地部署，以替换具有高历史错误密度的代码段（例如复杂的数据解析器、图像编解码器和字体堆栈）。
  • 实现高权限模块化。 通过用 Rust 编写新的模块化组件，Chrome 可以在高权限进程（如浏览器进程）内安全地执行复杂功能，而不会受到沙箱性能的影响，从而打破了传统 C++ 架构的限制。

除了 Rust 之外，我们还在探索使用 HTML、CSS 和 TypeScript 实现浏览器的顶级用户界面等选项，以进一步减少对传统 C++ 框架的依赖。

在安全漏洞落地之前发现它们

对代码库的批量扫描无法跟上 Chrome 高流量的开发速度。 考虑到这一点，我们还部署了人工智能驱动的错误查找功能，以尽可能在代码提交时间附近识别和防止错误。 作为 Chrome 持续集成 (CI) 和提交队列 (CQ) 管道的一部分，这些防御模型会自动扫描差异，通过执行建议跨度修复、标记悬空指针和强制数字安全等操作来防止新漏洞。

此外，大规模软件工程的一个主要挑战是“潜在的安全问题”。 孤立地安全且健壮的代码可能会因树中其他地方完全不相关的微小逻辑更改而转变为严重漏洞。 通过在 CQ 中利用由 LLM 支持的连续语义分析，Chrome 可以在这些复合风险登陆树之前拦截它们，捕捉传统静态分析错过的微妙或复杂的交互。

保护互联网安全

保持网络安全不仅仅涉及保护 Chrome。 Google 一直是开源项目和社区的长期支持者，以确保为所有用户提供更好的安全结果。 最近，Google 与其他公司一起向 Alpha-Omega 项目捐赠了 1250 万美元，以支持维护人员获得快速响应漏洞报告所需的工具和支持。 谷歌还是 Akrites 项目的创始成员之一，该项目旨在通过提供集中的漏洞报告交换所和安全事件响应团队来减轻上游维护人员的负担。

在 Chrome 团队中，我们强烈地感受到了这种责任——Chromium 项目是地球上最大的开源项目。 从这一挑战的规模来看，Chrome 在 Chromium 和卫星项目（如 V8 JavaScript 引擎、BoringSSL 加密库以及基础图形组件（如 Skia、ANGLE 和 Dawn））中拥有超过 2,300 个第三方依赖项。 其中约 1,700 个以一定容量交付给用户，融入从 Android 设备到边缘计算平台和大型云企业堆栈的各种产品中。

为了保持这些依赖项的修补，我们依靠自动漏洞扫描管道。 这些管道从 Google 的内部源以及多个外部监控源获取数据，包括美国政府的国家漏洞数据库 (NVD) 和专注于开源的开源漏洞 (OSV) 数据库。

现在，仅依靠反应性监控可能会留下危险的风险缺口，这一点比以往任何时候都要严重。 由于掌握漏洞及其补丁的最佳方法是保持第三方依赖项最新，因此今年，我们开始将所有 Chrome 第三方依赖项转移到自动更新管道上，主动将它们滚动到最新的上游版本。 自动化总是需要护栏，因此我们还将使用来自 Google 开源安全智能平台 (GOSSIP) 等项目的安全信号，以确保我们考虑到第三方开源软件生态系统中的其他风险。

前进

虽然法学硕士带来的软件安全方面的巨大变化可能令人震惊，但发现和修复的错误数量增加并不意味着失败。 每发现并修复一个错误，都会让攻击者少一个立足点。 但发现和修复错误只是成功的一半——我们还必须比对手利用错误的速度更快地为用户提供修复和应用更新，并投资于通过加快发布节奏、动态修补和适时重启来减轻或消除错误类别的项目，我们正在推动浏览器在不干扰用户的情况下受到持续保护。

不可否认，人工智能时代加剧了软件安全威胁形势，但通过将快速部署机制与深层结构防御相结合，我们正在确保防御者牢牢占据优势。 有了这个，Chrome 和更广泛的网络随着每次更新而变得更加安全。
